Freebuff: The free tier of the Codebuff AI coding assistant: a CLI, a web app and a desktop app that let developers code with AI at no charge, funded by first-party text ads.
Codebuff: The paid product line the Freebuff code lives alongside; the CLI ships as codebuff (1.0.x line) and freebuff (0.0.x line).
Freebucks: Pay-as-you-go compute credits a developer can buy to run models beyond the free allowance.
free model picker: The list of AI models a Freebuff user can choose from at no charge; it is published as the model table in the README.
provisioned tier: An early-access model tier granted to specific accounts; its models are not shown in the public picker.
limited offer: A capped free trial of a premium model, admitting a fixed number of sessions and one session per user.
waiting room: The screen a user sees when a capped model is full, showing how many premium sessions remain.
base2: The default orchestrator agent that plans a task and delegates parts of it to helper agents (researchers, reviewers, a terminal runner).
root agent: The agent a session starts with; helper agents it spawns are subagents.
agent registry: The public catalog of agents published by other people that the CLI can download and run.
trusted publisher: An agent author whose downloadable agents are allowed to run their own code; anyone else's runnable agents are refused unless the user opts in.
steering variables: Environment variables (CODEBUFF_*, FREEBUFF_*, NODE_OPTIONS and similar) that can change where the CLI connects or how it loads code; a cloned repository is not allowed to set them.
placements: Ad slots in the Freebuff interfaces that advertisers buy; placement caps and budgets apply to advertisers, not to developers.
sponsored proposal: An advertiser-funded task run by the assistant against a real repository, verified against a checklist the advertiser agreed to.
Conversions API (CAPI): A server-to-server channel that tells an ad platform (Meta, Reddit, X, TikTok) that an ad led to a signup, respecting Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control.
Axiom: The log and telemetry store the Freebuff service writes events to; changes there affect dashboards, not users.
direnv: A tool that loads a repository's .envrc file into the shell; the CLI reads it but drops any variable that could redirect or hijack the assistant.
MCP: Model Context Protocol: a standard way to plug external tools into the assistant.
snapshot commit: A public commit that squashes several private changes into one; the changelog reconstructs what it contains from the diff.
off-peak pricing: Cheaper Freebucks rates during hours when the service is less busy.
